name: HE Zlatoličje
description: Named in ZAG material as one of the hydroelectric plants where ZAG expansive and non-shrink grouts were applied. The plant works from a diversion canal rather than directly on the Drava channel. ZAG also lists third party quality control of the materials used in the upgrading of the Zlatoličje HPP, for Dravske elektrarne Maribor, 2006 to 2009.
history: HE Zlatoličje is the most powerful hydroelectric plant in Slovenia and was the first canal type plant built in the former state. Water is taken from the Drava at the Melje weir in Maribor and carried 17.2 km along a trapezoidal intake canal, largely on embankment, to the powerhouse near Zlatoličje, then returned to the Drava through a 6.2 km outflow canal cut deep into the ground. Between 2006 and 2013 both turbines and both generators were replaced along with the primary and secondary electrical equipment and the control systems, all six gates of the Melje weir were raised, and the dam and spillway wall were structurally reinforced. The replacement runner fitted to unit 2 has a diameter of 5,894 mm and a mass of 96 tonnes. Installed flow rose from 450 to 530 cubic metres per second and installed capacity rose by 12 MW. The small plant MHE Melje, running on the ecological minimum flow, entered service in January 2009.

source_differences: Installed capacity disagrees across sources: 136 MW (record 'typ', en.wikipedia Zlatoličje article), 126 MW (power-technology, record facts), 114 MW (en.wikipedia list of power stations, probably pre-refurbishment), max 133.2 MW (UM thesis 2009). Record 'typ' (136 MW) and 'facts' (126 MW) contradict each other.
Commissioning: power-technology gives commercial operation 1968, record gives first unit trial 19 Oct 1968 and official opening 26 Apr 1969 (compatible). Wikipedia: 'opened in 1969'.
Refurbishment dates: record 2006-2013, power-technology 2007-2012, Hydropower & Dams 2008 article describes it as ongoing.
'crosses: Drava' is misleading: the powerhouse is on the derivation canal (Hidroinštitut paper calls Melje/Zlatoličje a derivation-type plant).
power-technology lists 'gross head 33 m, net head 5.9 m', which looks internally inconsistent, not used.
The same source gives two units of 79 MW each, which adds up to 158 MW, not 126 MW.
Installed capacity: 136 MW (wiki.riteme.site) against 126 MW Zlatoličje hydro project (balkangreenenergynews.com)
Installed capacity: 136 MW (wiki.riteme.site) against 114 (list row 'HPP Zlatoličje | Drava | Zlatoličje | Run-of-river | 114 | 1969-') (en.wikipedia.org)
